sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s dive into arrays - your first step to handling multiple values like a pro!

• What arrays are and why they’re useful
• How to create and use arrays in Java
• Common mistakes to avoid when working with arrays

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine an array like a row of mailboxes at an apartment building. Each mailbox:
- Has a number (its position/index)
- Can hold one item (a value)
- All mailboxes are the same size (same data type)

Arrays work the same way! They let you store multiple values of the same type under one name. Instead of creating 10 separate variables for 10 numbers, you can create one array that holds all 10.

• Declare an array with `dataType[] arrayName`
• Initialize with `new dataType[size]`
• Access elements using `arrayName[index]` (remember: indexes start at 0!)

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Declare an array with: dataType[] arrayName (e.g., int[] scores)
Create an array with: new dataType[size] (e.g., new int[10])
Initialize with values in braces: int[] nums = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
Access elements using the index: scores[0] is the first element
Array indices range from 0 to array.length - 1; out-of-bounds access throws an exception

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Arrays let you store multiple values of the same type together. Always remember: array indexes start at 0. Practice declaring, initializing, and accessing array elements.
